old: Folic acid doses: prevention of neural tube defects = 400 mcg (0.4 mg) daily (start before conception and continue for first 12 weeks). Treatment of folate deficiency = 5 mg daily. Higher dose (5 mg daily before conception and for first 12 weeks) is recommended for women at high risk of NTDs (prior NTD, diabetes, obesity, antiepileptics).
new: Folic acid doses: prevention of neural tube defects = 400 mcg (0.4 mg) daily (start before conception and continue for first 12 weeks). Treatment of folate deficiency = 5 mg daily. Higher dose (5 mg daily before conception and for first 12 weeks) is offered to women at increased risk of NTDs (NICE NG247: personal, partner or family history of NTD, previous affected pregnancy, type 1 or type 2 diabetes, sickle cell disease or thalassaemia, antiepileptic or HIV medicines). A raised BMI alone does not need more than 400 mcg.

old: CURB-65: Confusion, Urea >7, RR ≥30, systolic BP <90 or diastolic ≤60 mmHg, age ≥65. Score 0-1 = home, 2 = consider admission, ≥3 = admit.
new: CURB65: Confusion, Urea >7 mmol/L, RR ≥30, systolic BP <90 or diastolic ≤60 mmHg, age ≥65. NICE NG250: 0–1 = consider discharge home with primary care follow-up and safety-netting; 2 = consider a virtual ward, SDEC unit, hospital at home or inpatient care; ≥3 = consider inpatient care, with critical care referral if appropriate.

old: CURB-65 ≥3: admit and treat with IV antibiotics.
new: CURB65 ≥3: admit; give IV antibiotics when the person cannot take oral medicines or severity requires it (as here), and review IV treatment by 48 hours (NICE NG250).

new: B. C. Antibiotics should not be delayed awaiting culture results. D. Focal consolidation with productive cough suggests bacterial pneumonia; antivirals are not routine. E. Insulin treats hyperglycaemia.

old: NICE guideline NG158 recommends direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) as first-line treatment for confirmed DVT. Rivaroxaban (15 mg twice daily for 21 days then 20 mg once daily) or apixaban (10 mg twice daily for 7 days then 5 mg twice daily) are both licensed and recommended. Treatment duration is at least 3 months. After 3 months, reassess for ongoing risk factors — provoked DVT (reversible cause, e.g., surgery) may stop at 3 months. Unprovoked DVT or continuing risk factors warrant extended anticoagulation (up to 6 months or indefinitely).
new: NICE guideline NG158 recommends direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) as first-line treatment for confirmed DVT. Rivaroxaban (15 mg twice daily for 21 days then 20 mg once daily) or apixaban (10 mg twice daily for 7 days then 5 mg twice daily) are both licensed and recommended. Treatment duration is at least 3 months. After 3 months, reassess for ongoing risk factors — provoked DVT (reversible cause, e.g., surgery) may stop at 3 months. After an unprovoked DVT, consider continuing anticoagulation beyond 3 months, often long term, based on the risk of recurrence versus the risk of bleeding and the patient's preference (NICE NG158).

old: Duration of anticoagulation for DVT: provoked DVT (surgery, immobility, pregnancy) = 3 months. Unprovoked proximal DVT or PE = 3 to 6 months (consider extended based on bleeding risk and patient preference). DVT or PE in active cancer = anticoagulation (usually a DOAC, or LMWH if a DOAC is unsuitable) for 3 to 6 months, then review whether to continue.

old: Indications for referral/further investigation: complex cyst (septations, solid areas), symptoms, simple cyst >70 mm, or persistent/enlarging 50–70 mm cyst. RMI (threshold 250) is used for postmenopausal women (NICE CG122).

old: Features of a concerning ovarian cyst requiring further assessment: complex (solid components, thick septations, papillary projections), bilateral, large (above 7 to 10 cm), associated with ascites or raised CA-125, or in a postmenopausal woman where any new cyst requires investigation.
